runs.v: Maine Venture Fund's typical position is roughly $400,000 built over time, two orders of magnitude below what a maritime autonomy or advanced manufacturing company needs to reach a program of record.

Private venture capital does exist in the state. Gaven Capital lists defense and space among three stated investment areas, though its named portfolio is consumer marketplaces and platforms and the defense exposure it displays is a SpaceX logo. Corsair Venture Partners is an early-stage firm based in Portland backing founders across New England. Neither shows a defense hardware track record.

So the break is narrower than saying Maine has no venture capital. Maine has early-stage venture capital and no defense hardware venture capital. No firm in the state has led a Series A into a hardware-heavy, long-sales-cycle defense company, and that is the sentence the formation argument rests on.

There is no DIU office, no OnRamp Hub, and no NSIN physical presence within 100 miles of Brunswick Landing. The nearest NSIN activity is in Boston. Neither Maine nor New Hampshire holds a Defense Manufacturing Community designation. A Maine company must build its customer relationship out of state from day one.
Seven stages from research origin to a program of record. Maine's chain is complete and in several places strong through stage five. It breaks at stages six and seven.
